notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; 7-week-old female C57BL/6 mice, n=4/group, single ICV injection of 38.4 nmol (200 ug). readout_value is TBD because Figure 1B is a grouped bar chart in which the two day-7 peaks (group means of roughly 9 and 6.5 on the 0-15 tolerability axis) and the smaller day-14 to day-21 bars (roughly 1.5-2.5) could not be assigned to individual ASOs with confidence from the colour key. Late-ONSET CNS toxicity: signs appeared at least 3 days after a single central injection, persisted for 6 days or more and worsened over time. The authors emphasise this is distinct from acute toxicity - no acute neurotoxicity was seen with ASO1, ASO3 or ASO4, and the acute toxicity of ASO2 resolved completely within 1 day. Tolerability scoring system in Supplementary Table S2 covers consciousness, motor function (ataxia, strength) and appearance (posture, breathing, home-cage activity). No recovery/reversal phase was run: animals were killed at a scheduled time point or when they reached a humane endpoint, and signs were progressive up to that point, so reversibility is recorded as irreversible on the evidence available rather than demonstrated permanence.

Rodent ICV acute-inhibition scale (Supplementary Fig. S1B): 0 bright/alert/responsive; 1 mild gait impairment; 2 obvious impaired gait/hunched posture; 3 moves away after lifting; 4 does not move forward but upright; 5 lying on side, responds to tail pinch; 6 no response to pinch but breathing; 7 death. Grade mapping for this 0-7 ICV scale: 0->0; 0<s<2->1; 2<=s<4->2; s>=4->3. Reducing PS content in the wings (six PS linkages replaced by PO) lowered the score for most but not all sequences (abolished for ASO2, no significant reduction for ASO8).

source_table: Results, 'Acute neuronal activation response occurs following the administration of oligonucleotides into the CSF of mice and NHPs' (Fig. 2E/2F, retrospective internal database)
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; CLASS-LEVEL ROW across many ASOs. Signs include tremors, muscle twitches, clonic or tonic limb movements, salivation, self-biting, opisthotonos and generalised convulsions or seizures; onset immediately after dosing or during anaesthesia recovery with full resolution after ~120 min and no apparent sequelae; diazepam alleviates the signs. Graded 3 because the authors state that, if severe enough, this response can be a DOSE-LIMITING finding in NHP. Animals over 4 kg were less likely to be affected. The 50 mg threshold is the dose above which the authors state the response is frequently observed.

effect_vs_control: Group 1: a NON-ADVERSE transient absence of lower spinal reflexes. It occurred at low incidence in untreated animals and in animals injected with artificial CSF; the incidence increased in ASO-injected animals and appeared to increase with dose. Reflexes were present again at 24 or 48 hours after dosing.
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; CLASS-LEVEL ROW aggregating 28 intrathecal cynomolgus monkey safety studies in 1,016 animals; per-compound and per-dose incidences are not given. SOURCE LIMITATION: only the abstract could be fetched (International Journal of Toxicology 2020;39:505-509 is not open access and no PMC record exists), so no figure, table or body-text number is claimed - dose, incidence and denominators are TBD. This is the single most compound-diverse NHP intrathecal neurotoxicity source found in this lane and is worth re-acquiring in full text.

effect_vs_control: 1/4 at 2 mg/animal vs 0/4 in the concurrent aCSF control group
source_table: Table 1 (microscopic observations), cervical spinal cord rows; narrative in sections 3.14.1 and 3.14.3
notes: [nonclinical] grade_provisional; incidence pooled across the 2 males and 2 females examined at each dose level (severity graded minimal/slight/moderate; counted here as present vs not present). Tissue: cervical spinal cord. 13-week GLP toxicity study in cynomolgus monkeys (2 males + 2 females per dose group, so n=4 per dose). aCSF vehicle control or 1, 2 or 4 mg NVP-13 per animal given intrathecally at L4/L5 on days 1, 15, 29, 43, 57, 71 and 85 (0.5 mL CSF removed first, 0.75 mL injected over ~1 min, 0.25 mL aCSF flush). A separate recovery group was necropsied after a recovery phase. NOAEL stated as at least 4 mg/animal. Authors' interpretation: mononuclear infiltration occurred at all dose levels with NO dose relationship, was perivascular and mostly meningeal, and was highest at the lumbar cord/injection site; gliosis and slight demyelination were attributed to the dosing procedure rather than the test item; minimal DRG neuronolysis was seen in a few treated animals but also in a recovery control and is known to occur spontaneously. Recovery-group necropsy showed the same pattern of CNS changes but with generally lower incidence and/or intensity, which the authors interpret as ongoing recovery - hence partially_reversible.
